### What does this PR do?

Replace three independent Ulysses Q/K/V all-to-all calls with one packed
collective when all three tensors have the same shape, dtype, and device. Q/K/V
are concatenated along dimension zero, redistributed once, and returned as
split views.

path. This reduces collective launches from three to one; it does not reduce
the communicated bytes and temporarily increases HBM usage for the packed
buffer.

support.

items.title: [model] fix: treat position_ids as optional in Ulysses input slicing
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

Ulysses sequence parallelism crashes instead of running when the caller does not pass
`position_ids`.

`patch_vlm_for_ulysses_input_slicing` decides whether to slice based on `inputs_embeds` alone,
then slices `position_ids` unconditionally:

```python
slice_now = (
    inputs_embeds is not None
    and current_ulysses_sp_size > 1
    and getattr(self, "_needs_initial_slice", True)
)
if slice_now:
    call_kwargs["inputs_embeds"] = slice_input_tensor(inputs_embeds, dim=1, padding=False)
    call_kwargs["position_ids"] = slice_input_tensor(position_ids, dim=-1, padding=False)
```

`position_ids` is optional in transformers — omit it and the model derives positions from the
sequence length it is handed. `slice_input_tensor` reads `x.size(dim)` on its first line, so
omitting it gives:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'
```

Minimal reproduction, with the wrapper installed on a stand-in module and slicing done without a
process group:

```
inputs_embeds + position_ids   ->  (1, 64, 8) -> (1, 32, 8),  (1, 64) -> (1, 32)     ok
inputs_embeds only             ->  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'
```

`patch_vlm_for_ulysses_input_slicing` is installed for `qwen2_vl`, `qwen3_vl`, `qwen3_vl_moe`,
`glm4v`, `kimi_vl`, `qwen3_5` and `qwen3_5_moe`, so this is on the shared sequence-parallel path
rather than one model's.

### The change

Slice `position_ids` only when there is one. Nothing else moves.

Leaving it unsliced is also the correct value rather than a workaround: the embeddings passed
down are already this rank's shard, so positions the model derives from their length are exactly
the ones this rank should see. Slicing a full-length `position_ids` and slicing nothing both end
at the same per-rank positions; the difference is only whether the caller supplied them.

items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

**Summary.** On hybrid models that carry an EAGLE-style sliding-window draft group (DFlash/DSpark-shaped drafters), that group hashes `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) + 1` block ids at *every* prefix-cache boundary and frees them *cached* onto the protected tail of the one LRU that all groups share, while — once it is exempted from the hit `min` — contributing nothing to the reconciled hit length. On a GLM-5.3-Flash deployment this one group spends 87% of the prefix cache and caps coexisting conversations at ~50K tokens each. A per-group retention interval, combined with exempting such hit-inert groups from the hit `min`, restored ~4× the coexisting-conversation capacity with the fine hit grid kept for the target model's groups, and a third party reproduced 99.95% cached across alternating 120K conversations. All numbers below are **deployment evidence from a vLLM fork**, not upstream verification; the code reading is against upstream `main` @ `22df3a3`. This RFC asks for agreement on the policy before any code is posted as a PR.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool 32-page split (hybrid block_size=1152) GPU Memory access fault on MTP decode
items.bodyExcerpt:
ROCm gfx942, GLM-5.3-Flash, hybrid KDA + MLA + kpool indexer: after the hybrid aligner lands on `cache_config.block_size = 1152`, the kpool indexer virtually splits 288-entry storage into **32-entry** paged-MQA pages. MTP decode then dies with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N` (one `VllmWorker` abort → engine down). Not OOM.

Line numbers below are **vLLM `main` @ `156050598eea0bb1124b9c106b22ba4a8c56f82a`** (2026-09-04). Runtime numbers are from a gfx942 serving image derived from #53906 plus later local patches; they are labelled as such.

## Environment (runtime)

- 8× MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3
- GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=4, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=2`
- Hybrid KDA + MLA + kpool indexer (`index_kpool = 4`)
- Serving image: #53906-era tree. Crash B already included the V2 slot-mapping `in_range` guard from #54296.

## Symptom

Two serving aborts on 2026-09-03, same family:

- Crash A (03:41Z): ~41054 computed tokens, first MTP decode after that prefill. Image did **not** yet have the #54296 V2 guard.
- Crash B (09:18Z): 5-way mixed batch (4 MTP decode + one 2304-token chunked prefill). `new_block_ids` around **3809–3813**. Prefix-cache hit ~93%, KV usage ~4.25%. Image **already had** the #54296 V2 guard.

Banner is `Memory access fault by GPU node-N` → that rank’s `VllmWorker` exits → engine down. Not OOM. An aiter GEMM-shape miss in the same logs is not sufficient (same shape had been served earlier without abort). `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens=[-1,-1]` is the async placeholder, not the address.

## Why 1152 becomes a 32-page split

`PAGED_MQA_PAGE_SIZES = (32, 64)` (`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:35`).

`Glm5NextIndexerCache.get_kv_cache_spec` (`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py:145-152`; there is no `amd/attention.py` sibling) picks the virtual page as:

- native if `storage_block_size <= 64`
- 64 if `storage_block_size % 64 == 0`
- **else 32**

On this host the hybrid mamba aligner set `block_size = 1152`. With `index_kpool = 4`:

`1152 / 4 = 288`, `288 > 64`

items.title: fix(anthropic): resolve model chat template before deciding inline-system merge
items.bodyExcerpt:
## What & why

When a client (e.g. Claude Code) appends a `system` message to the `messages` array of a `/v1/messages` request, the Anthropic compatibility layer can trigger a full prompt recompute (observed as a ~75s TTFT spike) because the entire prefix-cache block chain is invalidated from the system block onward.

**Root cause:** `AnthropicServingMessages.__init__` calls `self._detect_merge_inline_system(chat_template)` with the raw `--chat-template` arg, which is `None` by default. The detector returns `True` ("merge inline system into the leading block") whenever the template is falsy — even for templates like GLM that **already accept mid-conversation system messages**. That merge hoists the trailing system message into the leading system block, changing tokens from offset 0 onward and breaking the chained block hash (`hash_block_tokens` chains `parent_block_hash` into every block), so every subsequent block's hash changes → full recompute.

This builds on #44283 / #44602 / #46025, which introduced the merge-vs-inplace switch but defaulted to the conservative (merge) path. This PR closes the gap: resolve the model's actual chat template (the same `resolve_chat_template` call the renderer uses) before deciding, so GLM-like templates are treated as "no merge" and a trailing system message no longer destroys the prefix.

## Changes

`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`
- `__init__`: when `chat_template is None`, resolve the model's actual template via `resolve_chat_template(tokenizer, None, None, model_config=...)` (tokenizer from `self.renderer.tokenizer`), then feed it to `_detect_merge_inline_system`. items.title: HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA decode hot-buffering + GLM-5.2 indexCache opts (vLLM v0.24.0)
items.bodyExcerpt:
A port of SGLang's [HiSparse](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-04-10-sglang-hisparse/): full sparse-MLA KV lives in pinned host memory, decode is served from per-request GPU hot buffers holding the indexer top-k working set. Plus GLM-5.2 indexCache plan-once sharing and overlapped prefetch, which do not exist in the SGLang implementation.

**Motivation.** GLM-5 decode instances run wide-EP (DP×EP, one single-GPU engine per rank): each rank replicates attention/dense weights and carries its expert shard, DeepEP buffers, and sparse-stack workspaces — leaving O(10 GiB) of GPU KV per rank, a single-digit ceiling of long-context requests per engine (MLA's single latent head means KV cannot be TP-sharded away). In a P/D deployment that ceiling back-pressures prefill and stalls the pipeline. Sparse MLA only attends to the indexer's top-k (2048) tokens per step, so the full KV does not need to be GPU-resident.

## Results

**16-node production stack** (GLM-5.2-FP8, 8 prefill + 8 decode nodes, DP64 wide-EP decode, llm-d router, NIXL P/D, Mooncake prefill store, 160 GiB pool/rank):

- **26,056 decode tok/s sustained** at 5,173 avg / 6,092 peak of 6,144 seats (99% peak occupancy), ITL p50/p95 201/294 ms, **zero preemptions**, host pool 62% peak — 3.3× the same stack's throughput at c=1000. The binding constraint was the configured seat cap (`max_num_seqs=96` × 64 ranks), not compute, pool, or prefill (which sat nearly idle under shortcut routing).
- **A/B vs plain GPU-KV decode** — identical topology, traffic, and 50-min saturated measurement window; per-engine cumulative deltas over all 128 engines:

| decode side | GPU-KV | HiSparse |
|---|---|---|
| generation throughput | 10,653 tok/s | **12,951 tok/s** (+22%) |
| requests completed | 84,026 | **101,653** (+21%) |
| preemptions | 5,174 | **0** |
| TTFT p99 | 99.9 s | **2.5 s** |
| queue time p99 | 101 s | **0.8 s** |
| local prefix-cache hit | 40.4% | **92.2%** |
| NIXL transfer volume | 26.5 TiB (326 MiB avg) | **7.0 TiB**

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Fused DSA indexer Top-k kernel (LiteTopk)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## 📌 Description

Hi @youkaichao @WoosukKwon @mgoin @hmellor @njhill @Isotr0py @DarkLight1337, could you please take a look at this PR when you have a chance?

This PR introduces two complementary SM100 prefill optimizations for DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA):

- **LiteTopK** accelerates the indexer by fusing MQA scoring, online filtering, and TopK selection without materializing the `[num_q, seq_len]` score matrix.
- **LiteDSA** further accelerates the subsequent sparse-attention computation by packing multiple neighboring queries into one larger masked attention GEMM, reusing their heavily overlapping KV sets.

To the best of our knowledge, LiteTopk is the first Indexer-Topk implementation that avoids to store the score matrix, and LiteDSA is the first that converts multiple small per-token sparse-attention GEMMs into a grouped masked GEMM while preserving each query's original attend set. The corresponding paper is available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976).

**At 1M-token prefill, LiteTopK accelerates GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash by 1.29× and 1.08×, respectively. LiteDSA increases the end-to-end speedups to 1.40× and 1.25×, with no accuracy loss.**

Thanks to my collaborators Jianyang Gao ([@gaoj0017](https://github.com/gaoj0017)) from ETH Zurich, Peiqi Yin ([@yinpeiqi](https://github.com/yinpeiqi)) from CUHK, and Jiangneng Li ([@gravesprite](https://github.com/gravesprite)) from NTU.

DSA models such as **DeepSeek-V3.2/DeepSeek-V4**, **GLM-4.6/GLM-5.2**, and **LongCat-2.0** use a sparse-attention indexer during prefill. The current indexer computes an FP8 MQA score for every query/KV pair, materializes a `[num_q, seq_len]` matrix in HBM, and then runs a per-row TopK:

items.bodyExcerpt:
# Issue #49141 — Fused_moe dimension mismatch for Qwen MXFP4 model on ROCm

## 1. Root cause

The issue has two reports. Both are the same underlying defect: **a MoE layer whose
expert weights are stored *unquantized* in the checkpoint is still given a
*quantized* MoE method**, so the allocated parameters do not match the checkpoint
tensors.

The trigger in both cases is the MTP (speculative-decoding drafter) layer. AMD's
Quark and community GPTQ quantizations of `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` quantize the 40
transformer layers but leave the MTP layer's experts in bf16. The main model
loads fine; only the drafter fails.

* **Original MXFP4/Quark report** (`RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must
  match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1`, in
  `routed_experts.py::_load_w2`).
  `hidden_size=2048`, `moe_intermediate_size=512`. Quark MXFP4 allocates
  `w2_weight` as `(E, hidden, intermediate // 2)` = `(E, 2048, 256)` (fp4 packs
  two values per byte), while the checkpoint's MTP `down_proj.weight` is the
  unquantized `(2048, 512)`. `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`'s
  `quantization_config.exclude` lists `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.<i>.{gate,up,down}_proj`
  for all 256 experts, but `should_ignore_layer()` only compared the *parent*
  layer name `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts` against those *child* entries.
  **This half is already fixed on main** by the `check_children` argument added
  to `quark/utils.py::should_ignore_layer` (the amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 fix), which is
  why a commenter on the issue could not reproduce it on main. No change needed.

* **Still-broken GPTQ report** (issue comments:
  `AttributeError: 'RoutedExperts' object has no attribute 'w2_weight'. Did you
  mean: 'w2_qweight'?`, same drafter-loading path).
  `AutoGPTQConfig` tracks which modules the checkpoint actually quantized in
  `modules_in_block_to_quantize` — auto-derived in `maybe_update_config()` from
  the safetensors dtypes, so it contains only the quantized layers' per-expert
  module name

items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #29945

## The bug

With MTP or any other in-checkpoint drafter, startup prints two different max
model lengths for the same run:

```
[model.py:554] Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
[model.py:1684] Using max model len 131072
[model.py:554] Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP
[model.py:1684] Using max model len 262144
```

Users read the second line as the drafter being sized for a longer context than
the target and reasonably conclude that KV cache is being over-allocated. The
issue has collected repeat reports on Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and GLM-4.5-Air since
December, including cases where an explicit `--max-model-len 8192` still printed
`Using max model len 262144` for the draft.

@benchislett investigated twice and confirmed there is no over-allocation, since
`SpeculativeConfig._maybe_override_draft_max_model_len` clamps the draft to the
target immediately after the model config is built, and invited a PR to fix the
log.

## Root cause

`ModelConfig` for the draft is constructed with
`spec_target_max_model_len=target_model_config.max_model_len`, but
`_get_and_verify_max_len` only consults that argument inside the
`derived_max_model_len == inf` branch, which is the fallback for checkpoints
that declare no length key at all. Every real MTP or EAGLE checkpoint does
declare one, so the argument is dead in practice and the draft resolves to its
own declared length, logs it, and is only corrected one step later by the
clamp in `SpeculativeConfig`.

So the bound exists twice, in two different places, and the value that gets
logged is the one from before the bound is applied.

## The fix

Apply `spec_target_max_model_len` as an upper bound in `_get_and_verify_max_len`
whenever the length is being derived, so the draft resolves and logs the value
it will actually run with. The later clamp in `SpeculativeConfig` becomes a
no-op, which also stops its `Overriding draft model max model len` line from
firing on a config that was never wrong.

## Problem

`ParserEngineReasoningAdapter` forwards `is_reasoning_end` to its parser engine but not `is_reasoning_end_streaming`, so every parser-engine-backed reasoning parser falls through to `ReasoningParser`'s default:

```python
def is_reasoning_end_streaming(self, input_ids, delta_ids) -> bool:
    return self.is_reasoning_end(input_ids)
```

`should_advance` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:430`) calls this **once per structured-output request per decode step** while the request is still inside its reasoning block, so the scheduler re-scans the accumulated sequence every step. The adapter also did `list(input_ids)` on each call, materializing the whole prompt+output token sequence.

Resolving the MRO for the registered reasoning parsers, **17 of 30 inherit that default; 13 of them via this one adapter** — `qwen3`, `mistral`, `kimi_k2`, `minimax_m2`, `glm45`, `glm47`, `gemma4`, `deepseek_v4`, `inkling`, `ling3`, `mimo`, `nemotron_v3`, `seed_oss`.

## Measurement

Simulating exactly what `should_advance` does — `Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter`, one call per decode step over a growing reasoning block, `all_token_ids` as a real `ConstantList`:

| 1000 | 46.7 | 0.56 |

| 4000 | 202.2 | 0.56 |

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Bound the decode paged-MQA-logits sanitize to the top-k read region
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

After [vllm#49714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49714), every decode step runs `nan_to_num_(-inf)` over the full
`[rows, max_model_len]` logits workspace. On GLM-5.2 `max_model_len` is 258048,
so this costs 43 us per call regardless of how short the context is.

The top-k only reads the front of each row. This PR sanitizes just that slice
using a small Triton kernel, and falls back to `nan_to_num_` below 10M elements
where a kernel launch isn't worth it.

## Safety

- The sanitized region is a superset of what the top-k reads, so the result is
  identical.
- NaN/Inf handling matches `nan_to_num_(-inf)` exactly: NaN -> `-inf`,
  `+inf` -> `FLT_MAX`, `-inf` -> `-FLT_MAX`.
- The launch grid depends only on the row count (a shape), so CUDA graph capture

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #54744.

With `--reasoning-parser glm45`/`glm47`, passing `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` (or `thinking: false`) disables the parser's reasoning extraction. For GLM-4.5/4.6 that is correct, because their templates honor the kwarg and the model emits no think block. GLM-5.3-family templates read neither kwarg, so the model thinks unconditionally, and the raw scratchpad plus a dangling `</think>` lands in `message.content`:

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Simple question.</think>2 + 2 = **4**\n\n..."}
```

The fix is output-driven: when extraction was disabled but the output still carries a think block, split it with the thinking-armed engine config instead of passing it through. Tag-free output (a template that genuinely honored the switch) passes through byte-identically, so GLM-4.5/4.6 behavior is unchanged. The request-scoped engine keeps the unarmed config, so the streaming and id-space paths (`is_reasoning_end`, `extract_content_ids`) are untouched.

Scope boundary, stated plainly: the streaming path still cannot auto-detect this case, because by the time a dangling `</think>` arrives the scratchpad has already streamed. Auto-detection there would require buffering content for models that legitimately disabled thinking, which is worse than the leak. Operators hitting this should drop the ignored kwarg for GLM-5.3 deployments; the non-streaming leak this PR closes is the verified repro from the issue.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] Fix MoRI-IO KV block-offset for speculative decoding (MTP)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
`compute_block_transfer_offsets` in the MoRI-IO KV connector raised `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` whenever the producer's local block count exceeded the consumer's. Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** with `block_size=1`, the prefill (producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead slots that the decode (consumer) side does not allocate, so `local` exceeds `remote` by exactly the spec-token count (e.g. **8003 vs 8000** at n=3). This crashed the first prefill→decode KV write and made MTP unusable over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation.

## Fix
Block order is positional (`block_size=1`), so the prompt KV is the prefix and the extra local blocks are empty lookahead scratch. Clamp `local_block_ids` to `local[:len(remote)]` and transfer only the prompt prefix — symmetric with the existing shorter-local handling already documented in the same function.

## Tests
`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py`:
- Replaces the now-obsolete longer-local *raise* test with **clamp-to-prompt-prefix** tests for both the interleaved (`transfers_per_block=1`) and separated split-KV (`transfers_per_block=2`) layouts, asserting the result is identical to transferring `local[:len(remote)]`.
- Adds a shorter-local regression guard (pre-existing READ-mode partial transfer unchanged).

## Validation
GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP **1P1D / 1P2D PD-disagg** (vLLM v0.27.1 + AITER v0.1.19), MTP n=3:
- KV transfer succeeds (clamp fires, e.g. `8003 -> 8000` / `8 -> 5`); no more ValueError.
- Coherent output, **0 token-0 (`!`) corruption**, FULL cudagraph engaged.
- 8k/8k decode-heavy shows the expected MTP TPOT win (1.36–1.45×) at low concurrency.

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Saturate bf16->fp16 conversion in QuickReduce
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55345.

QuickReduce packs bf16 inputs into fp16 before the codec runs
(`quick_reduce_impl.cuh`, the `cast_bf2half` branch). bf16 covers the fp32
exponent range; fp16 stops at 65504. `__float22half2_rn` does not saturate, so
any activation above that becomes `inf` and propagates through the reduction,
poisoning the whole line — silently, with no warning and no numerical check.

The conversion sits *ahead* of the codec, so this affects every quantization
mode (INT4/INT6/INT8 **and** FP), not only the quantized ones.

## Test Plan

Two ranks on MI355X (gfx950), INT8 codec, one out-of-fp16-range value on rank 0
and 1.0 everywhere else:

```python
x = torch.full((n,), 1.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
if rank == 0:
    x[0] = 1.0e30           # representable in bf16, not in fp16
out = qr.quick_all_reduce(x)
print(out[0].float().item(), torch.isfinite(out).all().item())
```

Same container image in both runs, only the built extension differs, so the
difference is attributable to this change and nothing else.

## Test Result

```
before: out[0] = inf     torch.isfinite(out).all() = False
after:  out[0] = 65536   torch.isfinite(out).all() = True
```

Other elements unchanged at 2.0 in both runs.

End-to-end on GLM-5.3 (TP4, MXFP4 + fp8 attention, 8192-token chunks) the clamp
is not measurable against run-to-run noise — the surrounding loop is
bandwidth-bound and the two `fminf`/`fmaxf` pairs ride along in registers.

## Scope

This is a mitigation, not a complete fix, and I would rather state the limit
than oversell it: with N ranks each contributing a clamped 65504, the fp16
accumulation can still saturate. What it removes is the case where a single
out-of-range value destroys the entire reduction. Keeping bf16 end to end for
bf16 inputs would be the complete answer, but that is a larger change with its
own cost, and worth deciding separately.

items.title: [Bugfix] Detect NVFP4 in compressed-tensors mixed-precision checkpoints
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`ModelConfig.is_nvfp4_quantized()` detects NVFP4 by looking for `"nvfp4"` in the quantization config's **top-level** `format` string. Compressed-tensors **mixed-precision** checkpoints declare per-group schemes instead — the top-level format is `"mixed-precision"` and never names nvfp4 even when groups plainly are.

Concrete case: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (`format: "mixed-precision"`, `config_groups.group_1` = W4A4 float, `tensor_group`, `group_size 16`, per-group `format: "nvfp4-pack-quantized"`, targeting `mlp.(gate|up|down)_proj` — 56 of 64 MLP layers). The check returns False → `enable_act_fusion()` returns False → `pass_config.fuse_act_quant` stays False at **every** optimization level → `ActivationQuantFusionPass` never runs → the fused CUDA op `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` is unreachable (it is referenced only from that pass) and Inductor handles silu+mul+fp4-quant — which `enable_act_fusion`'s own docstring says it cannot: *"FP4 quant is always custom so Inductor cannot fuse it."*

Fix: when the top-level format is mixed, inspect `config_groups`. A group counts as NVFP4 if its per-group `format` names nvfp4, **or** it matches the NVFP4 scheme exactly (W4A4 float + `tensor_group` + `group_size 16` + symmetric), mirroring `CompressedTensorsConfig._is_nvfp4_format`. The strictness is load-bearing: **MXFP4 is also W4A4 float** (strategy `group`, group_size 32) — e.g. `INCModel3/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4-Mixed-CT-AutoRound` — and must not be misclassified. Non-dict (preset-name) groups are guarded; non-mixed formats never consult groups, so e.g. pure `mxfp4-pack-quantized` behavior is unchanged.

items.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend][Parser] Preserve text between GLM XML tool calls
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

  The Rust GLM XML tool parser entered a special post-call state after parsing
  the first `</tool_call>`. When ordinary text and another `<tool_call>` appeared
  in the same buffered chunk, the remaining buffer was consumed without
  producing the text or parsing the later call.

  Intermediate and trailing text is now preserved, later tool calls are parsed
  normally, and equivalent input produces the same event sequence regardless of
  chunk boundaries. The behavior also matches the Python GLM parser.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap glm5next video sampling knobs
items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #55726

## Purpose

`glm_sample_frame_indices` walks `duration * target_fps` candidates and
deduplicates only at the end, so `Glm5NextVideoBackend` sizes that walk from the
requested fps rather than from the clip. On a 2-frame, 1-second source it spends
857 ms and 156 MiB to return 2 indices.

This clamps `target.fps` to `source.original_fps`. No sampling rate above the
source rate can return frames the container does not hold, so the walk becomes
bounded by the frame count while the sampled indices stay identical.

## Why not a fixed ceiling

An earlier revision copied GLMGA's `_MAX_FPS = 30` / `_MAX_FRAMES = 2048`. As
@JaredforReal pointed out, that ceiling has no basis in the GLM-5.3-Flash video
processor: its `processor_config.json` sets only `fps: 2` as the default
interval. A fixed 30 would also halve sampling for a legitimate 60 fps request.

Clamping to the source rate needs no magic number, and it makes the `max_frames`
ceiling unnecessary: with fps bounded, `extract_t` cannot exceed the frame count,
so `max_frames=100_000` keeps returning 10_000 indices exactly as on main.

## Measurements

Serving image, calling the backend directly, 2-frame 1-second clip, `fps` and
`max_frames` set to the same value:

| requested | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 200 000 | 11.9 ms, +1 MiB | 3.1 ms, +0 MiB |
| 2 000 000 | 87.4 ms, +18 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |
| 20 000 000 | 857.5 ms, +156 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |

Output is unchanged in every case: 2 indices for the 2-frame source, 900 for a

items.title: [BugFix] Group GLM-5 hybrid KV cache specs (indexer/state roles) correctly
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM-5.3 hybrids mix 34 KDA (mamba-style) layers with 11 sparse-MLA layers whose caches carry **three roles**: the main MLA latent (`tokens_per_state=1`), the kpool indexer K pool, and the compressor state (`tokens_per_state>1`). Upstream grouping mishandled this mix in three ways:

1. `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` lacked `get_page_sizes()` / `get_num_layer_tuples()` accessors that the hybrid-layout path needs; add them.
2. The hybrid-grouping guard treated every non-MLA spec as ineligible, dropping the indexer/state specs out of the GLM layout; extend it to accept `KpoolTailSpec` / `SlidingWindowMLASpec` alongside `MambaSpec`.
3. The pad-consistency assert assumed no pads survive pre-grouping, which does not hold when smaller indexer pages are padded up to the MLA page size; relax it to "at most one distinct pad".

Also routes the GLM-5 tensor-layout path so the mixed groups resolve to the shared hybrid layout.

Companion of vllm-project/vllm-ascend#16005 (the kpool sparse-attention backend these caches serve).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — GLM-5 hybrid models group their KV caches correctly instead of falling back to a generic layout that over-allocates (observed: 23 GB vs the correct 441 MB per rank).

### How was this patch tested?

End-to-end on Atlas 910B3 with a 48-layer GLM-5.3 hybrid + official W8A8 weights: cache groups resolve to the GLM layout, the model serves with the kpool backend (GSM8K-level gate 12/12), and FULL graph capture works.

items.title: [Attention] Enable FA4 sparse MQA decode on Blackwell
items.bodyExcerpt:
This adds `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4` as the preferred backend for supported BF16 sparse MLA workloads at 16 or fewer query heads per rank on Blackwell; above that head count it stays opt-in. Decode batches use FA4 directly on the flat KV cache; batches containing prefill use FlashInfer. The backend maps request-local top-k indices to physical cache rows, passes each row's valid length to FA4, and registers the required warmup and selection logic.

Tests cover routing, backend priority order, per-row top-k lengths across the kernel's 128-wide index blocks, empty index rows and top-k buffers wider than the configured indexer width. The companion FlashAttention change supplies the decode kernel. The full GLM-5.2 TP4/TP8 serving comparison completed successfully; no model-quality evaluation was run.

Validation: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k 'fa4_sparse or (test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness and FlashAttnFA4 and auto and (mixed_small or large_q_pure_prefill or mixed_long_q))'` — 24 passed, 18 skipped. `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_priority.py` — 3 passed.

For Perf Results see PR in FA repo: vllm-project/flash-attention#195

AI-assisted. The September 7 upstream search found no matching open FA4 sparse-MLA integration PR; related platform-specific work does not provide this SM100 backend.

items.title: [CI] Reserve autotuning headroom for GLM TP2 PCP2 eval
items.bodyExcerpt:
# PCP autotuning OOM: mitigation candidate

Status: implemented and linted; **not GPU validated and not a merge-ready fix**.

The TP2/PCP2/EP GLM-5.2 NVFP4 case in [main build 87636](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87636#01a07f9c-18d7-4842-8ea3-de40c89c34c8) profiles successfully, allocates KV cache, then fails during FlashInfer autotuning. The stack is `compile_or_warm_up_model -> kernel_warmup -> flashinfer_autotune -> _run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs -> cutlass_fused_moe -> FusedMoeRunner::getWorkspaceInfo`. It requests 12.22 GiB on each B200 when only 7.67 GiB is free; the initial profiling reserved 33.46 GiB for KV cache at utilization 0.92.

The candidate adds `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` only to `GLM-5.2-NVFP4-TP2-PCP2-EP.yaml`. On a 178.35 GiB device this reduces the requested engine budget by approximately 12.48 GiB, leaving more space for the later autotuning peak. This is a capacity mitigation, not a correction to runtime memory accounting. The estimate is not proof that all tuning tactics or evaluation batches fit.

Batch size 32768, context length 4096, concurrency 100, TP2/PCP2/EP, backend, fp8 KV cache, model, all 1319 questions, accuracy threshold and tolerance remain unchanged. The separate TP1/PCP4 synchronization failure still requires #55499.

## Existing work

Open draft [#49115](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49115) proposes moving autotuning before profiling. It has merge conflicts, failed pre-run checks and no reported GPU test result, so it must not be represented as a verified B200 fix. The CI budget mitigation is distinct from that production runtime change. Searches for PCP memory and the exact TP2-PCP2 config found no matching open budget mitigation. [#55671](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55671) changes autotuning cache management and explicitly remains a no-op on pinned FlashInfer 0.6.18.

## Validation

- Applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check`: passed.
- YAML parsing and shlex argument comp

items.title: [vllm-bench, feature] Added support for Mooncake-style, timed-traces replay.
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Port `vllm bench serve`'s timed-trace replay to the Rust `vllm-bench` client: the `timed_trace` dataset (Mooncake-style JSONL: `{timestamp, input_length, output_length, hash_ids}`) and `--self-timed` scheduling, so recorded request-arrival schedules can be replayed faithfully from Rust. These 8 flags were previously allowlisted as `PYTHON_ONLY` in `rust/src/bench/tests/cli_parity.rs`; per that file's contract, this PR removes them.

## Example

```bash
vllm-bench \
  --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model glm-5.2-fp8 --tokenizer <tokenizer path> \
  --dataset-name timed_trace \
  --dataset-path trace.jsonl \
  --self-timed \
  --timed-trace-chunk-hash-size 16 \
  --timed-trace-sec-multiplier 0.001 \
  --num-prompts 1422
```

## Scope

Replays the shape of the traffic, not its content: arrival schedule, ISL/OSL, and prefix-sharing structure are preserved; prompt tokens are synthetic. Completions endpoint only. Complementary to #51104, which covers multi-turn HF datasets and intentionally excludes trace replay.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `timed_trace`, `self-timed`, and Rust bench trace replay: no open PR implements this.

## Test Plan

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p vllm-bench`
- Local schedule-fidelity check against a mock SSE server: 3-request trace with recorded offsets 0/2/4 s, with and without `--self-timed`.
- Live A/B against the Python client: same deployment, same 1,422-request agentic SWE trace (3,862 s recorded span), same nodes; only the benchmark client differs.

## Test Result

- `cargo test -p vllm-bench`: 170 passed, 0 failed (12 ignored: network). fmt and clippy clean.
- Mock-server fidelity: arrivals at 0 / 2.002 / 4.004 s with `--self-timed`; single burst with `--no-self-timed` (negative control).
- Live A/B:

| check | trace | Rust vllm-bench | Python `vllm bench serve` |
|---|---:|

items.title: [Perf] Keep P2P control requests moving during model steps
items.bodyExcerpt:
Addresses #55179.

Peer registration blocks the P2P session loop, and model execution delays control-message progress. Register peers asynchronously and service offload control requests on the scheduler thread while a separate thread waits for model output. Keep acknowledgements and teardown ordered.

No overlapping open PR was found. Native NIXL lock contention during registration is not eliminated.

## Tests

Tested `fab554afe1db` on 2× NVIDIA H100 80GB:

- Tiering regressions, model-wait regressions and a controlled registration-stall reproducer: **400 passed** (399 repository tests + one external reproducer). Baseline fails the four model-wait cases and blocks in the injected registration stall.
  `/workspace/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py /workspace/test_registration_progress.py -k 'not test_engine_core or model_wait' -q`
- Existing engine lifecycle/concurrent-batch tests: **2 passed**.
  `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn /workspace/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_engine_core tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_engine_core_concurrent_batches -q`
- Qwen3-0.6B, UniProc, NIXL 1.3.2, batch invariance enabled: **8/8** real P2P outputs match local prefill and baseline.
- Qwen3-8B, multiprocess, NIXL 1.4.1: **8/8** fixed P2P outputs match baseline; 2,048 remote cached tokens per request. Four concurrent 30k-token source requests provide background load, without injected delays.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed.

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Return closed Ling3 reasoning as reasoning in non-streaming
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Non-streaming `ling3` returns a closed reasoning block as `content` when nothing follows `</think>`. For the output `<think>reason</think>` the response has `reasoning=None` and `content="reason"`. Streaming `ling3` and the `glm47` parent return `reasoning="reason"` and `content=None` for the same output. The chain of thought leaks into the answer field.

`Ling3Parser.extract_reasoning` in `vllm/parser/ling3.py` demotes reasoning to content so that an unclosed `<think>` block (thinking budget or truncation) is reported as content. The demotion used `not content` as its trigger. That is also true for a fully closed block with no answer after it. The fix triggers on the absence of the closing marker instead. The existing `<tool_call>` guard is unchanged.

Expected semantics come from the parent's own test, `COMPLETE_REASONING` in `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py`.

Not a duplicate. No open PR or issue touches this condition. #55485 edits the import block of `tests/parser/engine/test_ling3.py`. The new test sits below that, so the rebase for whichever lands second is trivial.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_ling3.py -q
pytest tests/parser/engine -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/parser/ling3.py tests/parser/engine/test_ling3.py
```

Reproducer without a model:

```python
from tests.parser.engine.replay_harness import MockTokenizer, _test_request
from vllm.reasoning import ReasoningParserManager

vocab = {"<think>": 1, "</think>": 2, "<tool_call>": 3, "</tool_call>": 4,
         "<arg_key>": 5, "</arg_key>": 6, "<arg_value>": 7, "</arg_value>": 8}
parser = ReasoningParserManager.get_reasoning_parser("ling3")(
    MockTokenizer(vocab=vocab, tokens=[]))
print(parser.extract_reasoning("<think>reason</think>", _test_request()))
```

## Test Result

Before: `(None, 'reason')`. After: `('reason', None)`.

New test with the fix reverted: `1 failed, 6 passed`. With the fix: `7 passed`.

Full `tests/parser/engine`: `3836 passed`.

items.title: [Bugfix][CUDA] Fix the FlashInfer's fused all-reduce issue where NVLink multicast isn't available
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
Follow-up to #52861
That PR routes GLM DSA and DeepSeek V3.2 through the NVIDIA DeepSeek V3.2
implementations and adds them to `DEFAULT_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH_ARCHITECTURES`,
which sets `CompilationMode.NONE`. `fused_allreduce_rms_norm` now kicks into action so those
models now probe the FlashInfer workspace for every layer.
If NVLink multicast is not available for any reason, FlashInfer's fused all-reduce workspace can't be created, and the attempt fails with CUDA error 801.
get_fi_ar_workspace() caches only success: its early return is if `_fi_ar_workspace` is not None, so a failure is never remembered and every subsequent call re-issues a real fabric allocation. Callers handle the None fine by falling back to a plain collective, so the failures are harmless — until one of those retries happens on a stream that is capturing a CUDA graph. The failing driver call invalidates the capture, and the next allocation on that stream dies with `cudaStreamCaptureStatusInvalidated`. 

The fix is to cache the failures so that the later calls on the same config would return None immediately. Also to explicitly not create during graph capture (is_current_stream_capturing)

To replicate: Run GLM-5.2 or Kimi-K3, or similar on a multi-node GB300 (i.e. tp=8 on 2x4GPU) on 0.29 or above (0.28 works through the deepseek_v2 rather than vllm.models.deepseek_v32)

## Test Plan

Run the repro from above and verify the models start normally

## Test results
GLM-5.2 tp-8 over 2 nodes, MTP-5, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: fails in capture before,
starts after. Workspace attempts drop from 22 down to 1
